title: [R1 architecture] Attribute public row-store costs and select the execution redesign
body:
## Goal and primary output

Produce one accepted architecture/attribution decision for [#5090](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5090), with a concrete reuse/removal map, public API and lifetime contract, ranked causal limiters, implementation choices and predeclared cost budgets. Primary deliverable: **decision** published on this issue plus `TreeDB/docs/design/r1-row-execution-architecture.md` in a focused docs/instrumentation PR if needed. This is a bounded inquiry, not a prerequisite chain of separate research tickets.

## Questions and known facts

Separate (1) JSON/typed decoding and copying, (2) classic manifest and cold asset/offset work, (3) index derivation/old-state lookup, (4) publication resource cloning/checkpoint work, (5) actual fsync and serialization waits, and (6) harness/oracle activity. Confirmed mechanisms motivate the choices; historical 59.9 µs GetInto, 10–12 ms generic durable updates and 3.83 MB checkpoint allocation do not attribute their shares.

Trace Get/GetInto, prepared 32-row fetch, ordinary 10-row range, generic UpdateBatch, typed replace/upsert and meta.* preservation through existing public callers. Inspect current COW and Quicksilver merge/ownership state. Reuse `CommandWALRequestTiming`, publish timing/counters, existing immutable catalog and verified offset cache, including separate unbounded view block/held-offset retention; do not add a parallel profiler/authority framework.

## Bounded inquiry and recommended decisions

1. One phase/allocation campaign at a pinned current runtime. Use interleaved controls, setup/first-use/warm separation, serial versus admitted concurrent writes, and targeted scaling of rows, parts/manifests and revisions. Start from the existing 4,096-row fixture; select larger sizes and concurrency from available memory/I/O capacity. Change one dimension per diagnosis rather than a full combinatorial sweep.
2. Define exclusive top-level wall partitions; nested WAL/sync subphases are not additive. Attribute allocations by request/row/setup plus live retained ownership; distinguish DB code from fixture/oracle/SQLite C activity.
3. Prefer a shared captured row reader plus caller-directed emitter. Compare reuse of source-directory V2/certified point metadata against an incremental classic-manifest plan; retain checksum and generation/identity validity. A format change or persistent row directory is conditional on demonstrated nonlocal cold cost, not the default answer.
4. Prefer source-aware declared-string update plans retaining unchanged physical coordinates, with an explicit residual JSON contract and existing final-owner/index/WAL/publisher machinery. Keep callback UpdateBatch as the general fallback. Map #1186's broader plan seam without introducing multi-operation transactions.
5. Prefer finite identity-free preparation and existing ordered/durable-prefix primitives. Activate [#5094](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5094) only if prepare/serialization/sync attribution and actual eligible concurrency justify it; existing insert-only typed grouping is not generic update admission.
6. Select a resumable immutable revision inventory/scheduling protocol plus short fresh authority fences for [#5095](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5095). Show how corruption, directory rebind, new pins and concurrent publication invalidate scheduling without weakening exact deletion authority.
7. Assign the checkpoint allocation increase and active append retention to exactly one live owner: #5015/#5016 or a relevant new collection packet when causally covered, otherwise create a narrow residual child after establishing distinct cause. Require churn through meaningful segment rotation to decide active-file economics; five finite epochs are insufficient.

One bounded feasibility check per critical unresolved layout/authority choice is permitted. If contradicted, record the counterexample and revised choice; do not rerun the same investigation until a desired result appears.

## Decision contract and acceptance

- [ ] Pinned source/docs/public caller/eligibility/fallback map distinguishes source facts, measured causes and hypotheses.
- [ ] Exclusive CPU/wait/allocation evidence ranks limiters; unmeasured costs are explicitly unavailable, not assumed.
- [ ] Architecture specifies reader/plan representations, ownership, lock order, row locator and asset validity, ordered identity assignment, visibility, ACK and recovery walkthroughs.
- [ ] Baseline fixture/population/concurrency, identical commands, fresh-process repetitions and noise are frozen; quantitative read/mutation/publication/reclamation objectives and finite memory/queue/work budgets are justified before candidate measurement. Zero-allocation claims or arbitrary inherited caps are prohibited.
- [ ] Every parent bottleneck has one owner; #1887 sole emission scope and active COW/Quicksilver/MVCC owners remain protected.
- [ ] Revise [#5092](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5092)/[#5093](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5093)/[#5095](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5095), activate/retire [#5094](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5094) and any format/publication residual, add native dependencies for required accepted decisions/merged PRs, and update the parent gate ledger. A negative mechanism result completes only this inquiry, not the parent's performance goal.

Test-first exception: decision/docs and attribution-only instrumentation have no meaningful red speedup test. Protect them with characterization, exclusive partition arithmetic, counter selection and deliberately corrupted artifact/identity rejection. Instrumentation is performance-sensitive; report enabled overhead and public-route selection. Docs include the design, affected architecture/concurrency/profile contracts and performance-guide interpretation.


## Shared execution contract

Parent: [#5090](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5090). Planning base: `b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a`; recheck affected production paths and owners before implementation. Read the parent's semantic, performance, documentation and reassessment contract.

This is a **decision** packet. Docs-only work has no runtime effect; diagnostic instrumentation is performance-sensitive and needs enabled-overhead, selection and artifact-integrity evidence. Prove the real public caller → eligibility → optimized primitive → fallback, with path/work counters; helper-only timings are insufficient. First capture the named invariant failing for the intended reason, or record a justified characterization exception for a behavior-preserving refactor. Run affected races, recovery/reopen and fault tests. Compare identical before/after commands and equivalent returned data, visibility, ownership and durable ACKs; report latency/throughput, B/op, allocs/op, setup/first-use, retained/peak memory and relevant storage/I/O/work counters. Charge allocations by row/request/batch/setup, and account for backing capacity and pins. Minimize avoidable copies/temporary representations before completion.

[#5091](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5091) freezes the workload, numeric objective/budgets and noise policy **before candidate measurements**, from phase-attributed baselines. Decision acceptance requires causal classification, selected implementable architecture and complete obligation/target ownership; it does not require a candidate runtime speedup. R/M/C/L own improvement gates. A negative mechanism result may complete this decision while the parent's product objective remains open. Unexplained material regressions block; an accepted necessary residual needs evidence, alternatives and explicit acceptance.

Use an isolated topic branch and PR; preserve unrelated work. Current repository policy requires a PR and strict current-head `TreeDB required gate`; the required formal-approval count is zero. Refresh rules before merge. Request credit-consuming AI review only for mature code/tests/performance evidence/docs, resolve findings, and repeat only for changed evidence. No execution or merge is performed by publishing these issues.

[UpdateBatch planning](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/api.go#L19224) reconstructs old complete rows before invoking a callback, then projects the replacement and derives index state. Revalidate old state/schema/conflicts at the authoritative commit boundary.
